name: Raelan Agle: Brain Retraining 101 and recovery-story channel
founders: Raelan Agle (MSW, former clinical social worker in medical settings; reports 10 years of ME/CFS then full recovery; Austin, TX)
founded_year_range: 2019-2024. The YouTube channel opened on 4 Sep 2019 and the book Finding Freedom came out about Dec 2019. Guest interviews began around 2021. Brain Retraining 101 launched in early 2024 (absent from the site in Dec 2023, on Teachable by Jun 2024), and the podcast followed on 21 Aug 2024.
cost_summary: The YouTube channel, podcast, 5-day starter email course and weekly cheat sheets are free. YouTube channel membership is optional at $4/month. Brain Retraining 101 costs US$197/month (may vary with local tax/currency), can be cancelled anytime and has a 14-day full refund window (Oct 2026). A $50-off code (BJORNFIFTY) appears in 2026 podcast show notes. The book is a low-cost Kindle/print title.
mechanisms: neuroplastic/learned pain (brain-generated danger signal / predictive processing)
autonomic/nervous system dysregulation (sympathetic overdrive, "stuck in fight-or-flight")
mechanism_summary: The programme holds that a protective nervous system gets stuck in protection mode and keeps generating real physical symptoms (fatigue, pain, POTS, MCAS) after the trigger has resolved. This learned, over-sensitive response is called a neuroplastic symptom. Fear, hypervigilance and suppressed emotion or pressures keep it going, and it can be unlearned by building safety. The same mechanism is applied to every diagnosis, and no biomedical secondary-dysfunction model is offered.
roots: Pain Reprocessing Therapy / Schubiner mind-body syndrome
mainstream_notes: This is a direct-to-consumer LLC with lay and peer coaches. Clinicians including Schubiner, Gordon, Garner and Mickel have appeared as podcast guests (confirmed in the RSS feed), but no health system uses the programme. Its graded-activity and retraining framing sits outside the NICE 2021 ME/CFS guideline, which advises against GET and Lightning-Process-type therapies.
insurance_notes: The programme is a self-pay subscription with no reimbursement pathway.

key_trials.citation: Cefai S. Recovery Report: What 75 YouTube Interviews Say About Recovery from Chronic Fatigue Syndrome and/or Related Illnesses. Goldsmiths, University of London, July 2026 (open-access report; peer review not stated)
key_trials.design: Qualitative analysis of 75 self-selected recovery interviews from Agle's YouTube channel; not a clinical trial
key_trials.finding: Per raelanagle.com/research, 77% self-described as fully recovered, 95% said mind-body ideas helped and 84% said nervous-system regulation helped. The sample was selected on recovery and recovery was self-reported, so the report does not test or validate the course.

controversy: The programme frames ME/CFS and long COVID as neuroplastic, retrainable conditions, which many ME/CFS patients and advocates reject as psychogenic and as carrying a risk of post-exertional malaise relapse from graded activity. The recovery-story format has strong survivorship bias, and the only 'research' analyses the founder's own selected interviews. The open-ended $197/month subscription with lay coaches comes with no outcome data, and the founder's training is in social work, not medicine. On the other side, the programme requires medical evaluation first and says it is not intended for people with mental-health conditions.

indicators.value: ~1.1K incl. shorts; nearly 300 recovery interviews (per raelanagle.com)
'millions of viewers each year'; 70K+ subs / 8M+ views on site

popularity.reach_estimate: Roughly 1M distinct people have been exposed to the free content (11M views, 81K subscribers). Paid enrolment is undisclosed and is probably in the low thousands.
popularity.method_notes: The trajectory is anchored on the YouTube join date (Sep 2019), the book (Dec 2019), the ages of key videos, the podcast launch (Aug 2024; 235 episodes by Oct 2026) and the July 2026 Goldsmiths report. Site counts that lag the live ones (70K/8M against 81K/11M) suggest continued growth. Reddit could not be sampled because it blocks automated access, and Google Trends and news were not checked, so the trajectory is coarse. cost_usd_typical assumes 3 months of subscription.
